meta.ancient_dna_source: Feigin et al. 2022, Science — University of Melbourne chromosome-level thylacine genome assembly
meta.proxy_genome_source: Tasmanian devil reference genome GCA_902635505.1 (Ensembl release 109)
meta.notes: Coverage and damage metrics reflect published assembly statistics. Edit burden extrapolated from Colossal Biosciences programme estimates and published divergence data.

ancient_dna_quality.interpretation: Excellent ancient DNA quality. Mean coverage of 47.2× and 1.8% contamination support high-confidence variant calling. Fragment length (78 bp) is within the acceptable range for well-preserved ancient specimens.

genomic_completeness.interpretation: Near-complete genome recovery. 94.3% of the extinct genome is covered at ≥5× depth. Coding (96.2%) and regulatory (88.7%) regions are well-represented, enabling confident divergence analysis across all functional partitions.

divergence.interpretation: Extremely high divergence (11.83% genome-wide, ~10.2 Mya). This far exceeds well-studied de-extinction pairs such as mammoth/elephant (~0.6%). The proxy genome is a distant structural template only; functional equivalence cannot be assumed for most loci. This is the primary biological constraint on feasibility.

edit_burden.interpretation: Prohibitive edit burden under current technology. 1,444,000 minimum functional edits — 144× current CRISPR throughput (10,000/project). At current rates: ~144 years. Feasibility requires an order-of-magnitude advance in genome editing throughput, potentially via base editing arrays or synthetic chromosome assembly.

ethical_ecological.interpretation: Mixed ethical/ecological profile. Positive factors: suitable habitat (moderate, 68,000 km²), apex predator niche unfilled since extinction. Concerns: 3 welfare flag(s) and 2 conservation conflict(s) require mitigation before a responsible programme could proceed.
